solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Went underground, keeping unwell, and moaned

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to cave is to explore caves, going below ground
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a cave while feeling sick and complains about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise petty objections, a form of complaining or grumbling.

clue.text: See 24
Bishop not good person, one not giving up quarrel

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letters for a good person are dropped

parts.note: a sticker is someone who persists and won't quit
ST, short for saint, is the crossword's good person

explanation.surface: A bishop is described as a bad person but a dogged one, in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ST (saint) from STICKER, leaving ICKER after B.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble over trivial things, a synonym of quarrel as a verb.

clue.text: West Country location prepared to collect sheaves of corn

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
an omer is a Hebrew word for a sheaf of corn, also a measure of grain

explanation.surface: A farm in the West of England gets ready to gather the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The omer is the sheaf of the biblical harvest offering, a word few solvers meet outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the south-west region known as the West Country.

clue.text: Spoil no child — scold, first off

parts.note: someone who is no longer a child is a grown-up

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to scold is to berate

explanation.surface: Advice on parenting: don't scold a child, it spoils them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops the B from BERATE, leaving ERATE after ADULT.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate food or drink is to spoil its purity by mixing in inferior substances.

clue.text: Fish — Cornish town gets rid of tons somehow

indicators.note: gets rid of means these letters are taken out of the town's name

parts.note: Launceston is a town in Cornwall, the county at the south-western tip of England
the letters of tons in some other order, here S T O N

explanation.surface: A Cornish town disposes of a great weight of fish in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rid of' takes STON, the letters of 'tons' in a new order, off the end of LAUNCESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: The launce is the sand eel, a small slender sea fish.

clue.text: Jewish expert and actors enthralling island

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A scholar of Jewish lore and a troupe of performers captivate an island audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbalist is a student of the Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition, hence an expert in it.

clue.text: Brown paintings maybe turning up in religious literature

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Brown-toned paintings appear among religious writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ART to TRA, after TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tantras are Hindu and Buddhist scriptures, sacred texts on ritual and meditation.

clue.text: Town's food beyond sell-by-date?

parts.note: food past its sell-by date is old
ham is a food

explanation.surface: A question about whether a town's food has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDHAM is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a former mill town near Manchester in north-west England.

clue.text: Group of our competitors getting a few minutes of broadcast?

parts.note: this puzzle ran in the Daily Telegraph, whose rival newspaper is The Times
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A team of rivals is granted a brief spot on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our' is the Telegraph speaking: its competitor is The Times, a rival British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is a scheduled period in a broadcaster's programming, often just minutes long.

clue.text: Almost stop royal mistress entertained by monarch being cooped up like a pet

definitions.text: being cooped up like a pet

indicators.note: entertained by means received within, so these pieces go inside the monarch's word

parts.note: king means monarch

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A monarch harbours his mistress, nearly bringing things to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts END to EN; with NELL, 'entertained by' puts ENNELL inside KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennelling a dog means keeping it shut in a kennel, confined as pets often are.

clue.text: Musical giant of the stage, the second one to go

indicators.note: to go means the named letter is removed from the actor's name

parts.note: Laurence Olivier was a towering English actor
one is the Roman numeral I; the second I in the name is the one dropped

explanation.surface: A great stage actor is in a musical, with a second actor dropping out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the second I of OLIVIER leaves OLIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage show based on Oliver Twist, a well-known musical.

clue.text: Disease expert is special visitor keeping record

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the record word goes within
special suggests something unusual, so the letters of visitor are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a record

explanation.surface: A medical specialist is a distinguished guest who keeps notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges VISITOR to VIROIST; 'keeping' puts LOG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A virologist studies viruses, the agents of many illnesses.

clue.text: What sounds like pleasant shelter for a cuppa

indicators.note: says the words below are said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: rosy means pleasant or promising; the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A question about a nice place to drink tea out of the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, the London dialect where a rhyming phrase stands in for a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, and the rhyming slang phrase means tea.

clue.text: Laugh at some of the dire drivel going round

indicators.note: going round means the letters are read in reverse
some of means only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: Mocking dreadful nonsense that keeps circulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes EDIRED from 'the dire drivel'; 'going round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, so it means laugh at in scorn.

clue.text: Unacceptable types, endlessly wicked, among five hundred workers

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: evil means wicked

explanation.surface: Wicked people with no end are found among a large workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims EVIL to EVI, which 'among' puts between D and ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviants are people whose behaviour departs from accepted social norms.

clue.text: Words of rebuke around about a king — beheaded one, maybe?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other letters are placed inside
around means turned the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tuts are clicks of disapproval
R, for rex, abbreviates king

explanation.surface: Someone tut-tuts over a king who might have lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses TUTS to STUT; 'about' places A and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles I, a Stuart monarch, was executed by beheading in 1649; Mary, Queen of Scots, too.

clue.text: Apple may make a contribution to this financial statistic

definitions.text: Apple may make a contribution to this financial statistic

parts.words: Apple may make a contribution to this financial statistic
parts.note: the tech firm Apple adds to sales figures; apple also makes a fruit pastry of that name

explanation.surface: Apple the company boosts a business number.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: the fruit pastry made with apple, and the sales figure Apple adds to.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's sales revenue over a period is a key accounting figure; an apple pastry folded over shares the name.

clue.text: American mogul's clubs perhaps

definitions.meaning: belonging to Donald Trump, the American businessman
in card games the suit that beats the others, clubs being one possibility

explanation.surface: An American tycoon's golf clubs, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the winning suit is called this, and clubs may be it; also the possessive of the mogul's surname.

clue.text: Show great respect, meeting sweetheart — wow!

definitions.note: an exclamation taken here as the verb to wow, impress greatly

parts.note: to bow is to show respect by bending forward
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone bows deeply on meeting their beloved, amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish or impress them, just as to wow them.

clue.text: They've got things woefully wrong, see, ignoring good English

indicators.note: woefully suggests something badly done, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring means leaving out these letters

explanation.surface: Some people have got things badly wrong, look, ignoring proper English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes G and E from WRONGSEE, leaving WRONSE, which 'woefully' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessors are people who have things, the holders of property.

clue.text: Happy exclamation concealing caution for the most part

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: a cry is an exclamation

indicators.note: for the most part means all but the last letter

parts.note: heed means care or caution

explanation.surface: A joyful shout hiding a note of caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims HEED to HEE; 'concealing' puts it inside CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheery means cheerful and in good spirits, a synonym of happy.

clue.text: Cook fish portion, having mislaid egg

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: having mislaid means this letter has been lost from the word

parts.note: a dole is a share or portion handed out
O, egg-shaped, is crossword shorthand for an egg

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a piece of fish but has lost the egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having mislaid' drops O from DOLE, leaving DLE after COD.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Mad manager, terribly muddled

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy boss is badly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes exactly what the wordplay does to 'Mad manager'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrammed letters have been jumbled up, i.e. mixed up into a new order.

clue.text: See 10
Regular undulation in audible signal? Ignore

indicators.note: audible means heard rather than seen, so the words below are said aloud

parts.note: a signal is a sign and to ignore a rule is to waive it

explanation.surface: A question of whether to disregard a wavy pattern in a sound signal.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGN sounds like SINE, and WAIVE sounds like WAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: This smooth periodic oscillation is the basic shape of a pure tone in physics.

clue.text: Toast experts having a drink

parts.note: pros are professionals or experts
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Specialists raise their glasses while drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in the British cocktail gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a drinking salutation from Latin meaning 'may it benefit', like 'cheers'.

clue.text: Writer as one who gives a toss when penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a slinger throws things
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author is a careless person who still writes an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives a toss' sounds like caring, but here it means throwing. 'penning' puts A inside SLINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.
